skill_entry.name: 14. A declaration, constant block, include or growing function sits where a reader will not look for it
skill_entry.trigger: Any one fires; all judged at HEAD. (a) A header hunk deletes or moves a line of a namespace-scope constexpr value block that existed at BASE below the file's first struct, class or function body; config headers (h/pos/config.hpp, h/system/config.hpp) are exempt. (b) A hunk adds a prototype, with no `-` twin of the same symbol in the hunk, to a header that exists at BASE, and the defining src/<dir>/<base>.cpp has a same-directory header h/<dir>/<base>.hpp other than the receiving one. (c) An added `#include "<path>"` where h/<path> does not resolve at the PR head and no src/**/<basename>.in generates it. (d) 30 or more added lines inside one function of 400 or more lines at BASE, split over both branches of one if/else. (e) A production header keeps 5 or more dump_/debug_/print_/trace_ definitions and another reviewer asked to keep them.
skill_entry.procedure: 0. A PR that creates the header, a branch merge or a workaround PR drew no placement comment; there (a) and (b) are noted, not reported. 1. Per touched header: first body line, constexpr value lines below it, constexpr lines the hunk deletes; home = top of file or h/pos/config.hpp. 2. Per added prototype: column-0 definition in src/, its same-directory header, the type whose members the body reads; a header without @file takes its topic from its name and first two structs. 3. Per quoted include: resolve at the PR head; list the library's sibling includes; read .clang-format IncludeCategories. 4. Per function with hunks: indentation-matched length at BASE and HEAD; added lines per branch. 5. Count dump_ definitions; look for a sibling *_dump.hpp. 6. Read non-bot threads and the body; a move request by another reviewer or a split the author schedules closes the item. 7. Report nits; never hold approval.
skill_entry.question: If a reader opens the file whose name says it owns this thing (the config header for a constant, the subsystem header for a declaration, the third-party include block for a library header, a helper for a long stanza), do they find it there, or do they have to search the body of a file about something else?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A constexpr block the PR creates or only extends (PR 1722 hwattention.hpp:162-171; PR 2135 added hwkv_tok_per_layer at :458, 0 lines deleted; both approved silently). A constexpr function or template tied to a type above it (PR 2774 mixture_of_experts.hpp:401, :409). One constant directly above its first user (PR 4353 model.hpp:131, used at :147). A block already at the top (hwattention.hpp:30-31) or in config.hpp. A re-spelled prototype with a `-` twin (PR 3756 debug_exit, get_device). A declaration in a header the PR creates (PR 1722 :24 `devices`). Pre-existing quoted includes (four at a62d15a3dc). `<ck_pr.h>` sorted by clang-format. A placement the body explains (PR 1980, 'good enough for now'). A split the author schedules. A move another reviewer requested. Debug helpers removed with nobody asking to keep them. Brace style, whitespace, include order inside a group. t/, .py, .txt, .json. PRs of 50 lines or fewer.
skill_entry.finding_shape: Declaration: Nit: `<symbol>` (<file>:<line>) sits next to `<neighbour>` in <header> and has nothing to do with <header topic>; its definition at <src file>:<line> reads <type> from <candidate header>. Odd place for it? Maybe `<candidate header>`? Constants: kinda pedantic, but can we move these constexpr (<file>:<a>-<b>, below `<first struct>` at :<c>) to the top of the file, or into <config header> with the other <group> constants? Include: a ```suggestion block with `#include <lib/x.h>` plus 'and group it with `#include <lib/y.h>` at :<line>?' Function: `<fn>` is already <N> lines at BASE and this grows the <A> and <B> branches by <n>+<m> lines; pull the two stanzas into helpers (name them; do not claim they are copies). Next iteration would be fine.
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: nit, in his words: 'just a nit', 'kinda pedantic', 'seems like an odd spot ... good enough for now though!', 'Next iteration would be fine though', 'That's something I could take on in a later iteration'. Minor at most for the long-function ask ('I really think we should'). He approved every member PR in the same review round: PR 1980 ten seconds after the comment (19:38:42Z comment, 19:38:52Z approval, both at 56d432ee61); PR 2176 the next day; PR 2980 three days later. He held nothing on these.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file at HEAD (line of the first body, include neighbours, dump_ share); other files (the definition in src/, the candidate header, config.hpp, .clang-format); BASE for the function length; PR body for a stated placement reason; other reviewers' and the author's threads on the same hunk.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: a declaration, constant block, include or growing function sits where a reader will not look for it

Common setup, in addition to the shared setup: for a merged PR, or whenever `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/main` prints HEAD itself, take BASE as the parent of the first PR commit: `first=$(gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json commits -q '.commits[0].oid'); BASE=$(git -C WT rev-parse $first^)`. When reproducing a comment, set HEAD to the commit shown next to the comment, not the final head.

0. PR kind: `gh pr view N --json title,body -q .title`. A PR that creates the header (`git -C WT diff --diff-filter=A --name-only BASE HEAD -- 'h/*.hpp'`), a branch merge or a workaround PR drew no placement comment in the corpus (1707, 1722, 1739, 2008, 2135 silent); on such a PR run steps 2 and 3 to note, never to report.
1. Touched headers: `git -C WT diff --name-only BASE HEAD -- 'h/*.hpp' > hdrs.txt`. Skip h/pos/config.hpp and h/system/config.hpp.
2. Constants (trigger a), per header F: `git -C WT show HEAD:F > full/F; first=$(grep -n -E '^(struct|class|union|template|inline|static|constexpr|[A-Za-z_][^;]*\))[^;]*\{ *$' full/F | grep -v -E '^[0-9]+:(namespace|extern|enum)' | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)` (first line that opens a struct, class or function body; a forward declaration `struct X;` does not match). Constant values below it: `grep -n -E '^(static |inline )*constexpr [^=(]*=' full/F | awk -F: -v f=$first '$1>f'`. Fire only when the hunk deletes or moves a pre-existing line of that block: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- F | grep -E '^-.*constexpr'`; no deleted line means no finding (PR 2135 added a line to the mid-file block and deleted none; PR 2176 deleted five). Candidate home: `git -C WT show HEAD:h/pos/config.hpp | grep -n -B2 'inline constexpr'` to find the group the constants belong to.
3. Declarations (trigger b): `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- 'h/*.hpp' | grep -E '^(\+\+\+|@@|[-+](extern|inline|struct|class|enum|template|[A-Za-z_:<>]+ [A-Za-z_]+\())'`. Drop a `+` line that has a `-` twin declaring the same symbol in the same hunk (PR 3756 re-spellings). Drop a header absent at BASE (`git -C WT cat-file -e BASE:H`). For each remaining symbol S in header H: `git -C WT grep -l -E "^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_:<>*& ]*[ *&:]S\(" HEAD -- src | sed 's/^[^:]*://'` lists the defining files (column-0 definitions only; call sites are indented). For each `src/<dir>/<base>.cpp` check `git -C WT cat-file -e HEAD:h/<dir>/<base>.hpp` (`h/<base>.hpp` when dir is empty). Fire only when that same-directory header exists and is not H. Confirm the candidate: `git -C WT show HEAD:src/<dir>/<base>.cpp | sed -n '<def line>,+30p'` and name the type whose members the body reads. Header topic: `git -C WT show HEAD:H | sed -n 1,20p` for `@file` / `@brief`; when there is none (h/pos/alloc.hpp has none), take the file name and `grep -n -E '^(struct|class|[A-Za-z_].*\() ' full/H | head -2`.
4. Includes (trigger c), resolved at the PR head, never at the worktree HEAD: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD | grep -E '^\+#include "' | sed -E 's/.*"([^"]+)".*/\1/' | sort -u | while read p; do git -C WT cat-file -e HEAD:h/$p 2>/dev/null || git -C WT ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD | grep -q "$(basename $p).in$" || echo "third-party quoted: $p"; done`. For each hit: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n -E '^#include [<"]<lib>'` lists the sibling includes and their lines; `git -C WT show HEAD:.clang-format | sed -n '/IncludeCategories/,/IncludeIsMainRegex/p'` (quoted = project group priority 3; `<lib/...>` = third-party priority 2; IncludeBlocks Regroup is what separates a quoted third-party include from its angle-bracket siblings).
5. Function growth (trigger d): `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- <file> | grep '^@@' | sed -E 's/^@@[^@]*@@ ?//' | sort | uniq -c` lists the functions with hunks; a blank or `extern "C" {` context is outside any function and is skipped. Length at BASE and at HEAD, indentation-aware so member functions count: `git -C WT show C:<file> > w.cpp; s=$(grep -n -E '^ *[A-Za-z_][^;]*\b<fn>\(' w.cpp | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); ind=$(sed -n "${s}p" w.cpp | sed -E 's/^( *).*/\1/'); e=$(awk -v s=$s -v ind="$ind" 'NR>s && $0 == ind"}" {print NR; exit}' w.cpp); echo $((e-s+1))`. Branches: `L=$(grep -n '<if line>' w.cpp | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); I=$(sed -n "${L}p" w.cpp | sed -E 's/^( *).*/\1/'); E=$(awk -v L=$L -v I="$I" 'NR>L && $0 == I"} else {" {print NR; exit}' w.cpp); E2=$(awk -v E=$E -v I="$I" 'NR>E && $0 == I"}" {print NR; exit}' w.cpp)`. New-side hunk starts b from `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- <file> | grep '^@@' | sed -E 's/^@@ -[0-9,]+ \+([0-9]+),?([0-9]*) @@.*/\1 \2/'`: b < E -> first branch, E <= b < E2 -> second branch; sum the added lines per branch.
6. Debug helpers (trigger e), per touched header: `git -C WT show HEAD:F | grep -c -E '^(inline |static )?[A-Za-z_:<>*&]+ (dump_|debug_|print_|trace_)[a-z_]*\('` and `git -C WT ls-tree --name-only HEAD h/<dir>/ | grep -E '_(dump|debug)\.hpp'`.
7. Threads and body: `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N/comments --paginate | jq -r '.[] | select(.path=="F") | select(.user.login | test("\\[bot\\]") | not) | [.id,.user.login,.in_reply_to_id,.body] | @tsv' | grep -i -E 'move|config\.hpp|belongs|odd place|top of|next (phase|iteration)|later|for now'`. A row by another reviewer that asks for a move closes the item (PR 2176: 2927506780 mcherba 'These probably ought to move to h/pos/config.hpp'). A row by the author on the same hunk that schedules the split or move closes trigger (d) (PR 2980: 3405422090 'planning this as part of the next phase'). Then `grep -n -i -E 'available wherever|for now|next (phase|iteration)' body.md` for a stated reason in the body (PR 1980).
8. Report each hit as a nit with the candidate home named; do not block.

On PR 2980 (BASE f59334dc24 = parent of 514fc3ec5f; comment commits edec446b76 and 247c8a4c22; final head a62d15a3dc): step 3 finds `extern void pos_driver_register_fuse_stats() noexcept;` at edec446b76:h/pos/alloc.hpp:234 under pos_devices_register_fuse_stats (:229, allocator stats; alloc.hpp has no @file comment, struct alloc_info :24, struct allocator :50); column-0 definitions in src/pos/device.cpp:595 and src/pos/fake.cpp:72; src/pos/device.cpp -> h/pos/device.hpp exists and is not alloc.hpp (fire); fake.cpp has no same-directory header; the body reads PosDevice counters at h/pos/device.hpp:404-405; the fix 7a139971bd moved the declaration to h/pos/device.hpp:662-665 at a62d15a3dc. Step 4 at 247c8a4c22 finds exactly `third-party quoted: spdlog/spdlog.h` (src/pos/device.cpp:12) with the sibling `<spdlog/fmt/fmt.h>` at :18, separated by `<pci/pci.h>` at :15; `system/fuse_stats_config.hpp` is cleared by src/system/fuse_stats_config.hpp.in; at a62d15a3dc both are angle-bracket and adjacent at :15-16 and step 4 prints 0 hits. Step 5: hw_prepare is 467 lines at BASE (src/pos/worker.cpp:1131-1597), 601 at edec446b76 (:1141-1741), 591 at a62d15a3dc (:1141-1731); hunks +1237(44), +1287(6), +1322(4) land in `if (!workreq->attn_req) {` (:1232) and +1361(56), +1419(14), +1452(10) in `} else {` (:1326-1462): 54 + 80 added lines; the author's reply 3405422090 defers the split and Wade approved at 10d44f7aba on 2026-06-15. Steps 2 and 6: 0 hits (device.hpp constants :30-40 sit above the first body `struct wqentry {` at :54). Step 7: 24 rows on the three files, 11 by cursor[bot], dropped by the filter.

On PR 2176 (BASE 1794cdf67d, comment commit 9553cd0a11; the inline comment carries commit_id 429249ead6, the child of the approval commit 8e19ea3e62, and its line 449 matches 9553cd0a11): step 2 finds first body `struct hwattn_kv_meta {` at :37 and the hwkv_* block at h/pos/hwattention.hpp:449-452; the hunk @@ -450,98 +448,9 @@ deletes five constexpr lines of the pre-existing block (header -928/+9), so (a) fires; PAGES_PER_WMEM and POS_PER_PAGE at :30-31 are above the first body. The fix 8a6db72438 (hunk @@ -446,11 +446,8 @@) removes 9553cd0a11:h/pos/hwattention.hpp:449-453 and adds the four constants as `inline constexpr` to h/pos/config.hpp:89-92 under the comment at :88 `// HW KV cache layout constants` (lines at 8e19ea3e62). Step 7 finds 2927506780 (mcherba, 2026-03-12) asking for config.hpp, which closes the item before Wade's ask.

Over the 15 silent PRs with diffs (heads from corpus.json): step 2 as narrowed fires on 0 (the first draft fired on 1722, 2135, 2774, 4353); step 3 as narrowed fires on 0 (the basename-only draft fired on 1722 and 3756); step 4 resolved at the PR heads fires on 0 (resolved at the worktree HEAD it falsely fired on 5 project headers of 1707 and 1722); steps 5 and 6 fire on 0.

final.precedent_note: n = 6 comments over 3 PRs (tron-1980, tron-2176, tron-2980), 2026-02-03 to 2026-06-12. Five are top-level inline comments; one (2948027543, PR 2176) is a reply to mcherba's request to keep the dump helpers. No member is pasted assistant text: none of the three PRs is among the nine pasted-text PRs (2233, 2461, 2872, 2906, 3008, 3490, 4128, 3879, 4191) and no member body names an assistant.
changes_made: Trigger (a) narrowed: fires only when the hunk deletes or moves a pre-existing constexpr line below the first body (precision lens). Executability proposed a hunk ratio (removes 5x what it adds) instead; both rules separate PR 2176 from the four silent PRs, and I chose the per-line rule because it is a fact about one line, not a threshold set from one example. Verified: `git diff -U0 1794cdf67d 9553cd0a11 -- h/pos/hwattention.hpp` deletes 5 constexpr lines (header -928/+9); `git diff -U0 71a22bddd2 f4d1f7d924` for PR 2135 deletes 0 and adds one at :458.

Trigger (b) narrowed by combining both lenses: the header must exist at BASE, the `+` line has no `-` twin (precision), and the defining src file's same-directory header exists and is not the receiving header (executability). Verified by running the step 3 command: fires on edec446b76 alloc.hpp (src/pos/device.cpp -> h/pos/device.hpp), does not fire on 7206e88cc2 debug_exit / get_device (src/pos/driver.cpp, fake.cpp have no h/pos twin) or scan (h/pos/device.hpp is the receiving header). The definition regex was corrected to column-0 matches so call sites in rinzler.cpp and runtron.cpp do not count.

Step 2 first-body command replaced with the executability lens form (line that opens a body with `{`, excluding namespace/extern/enum) and the constant regex restricted to values (`[^=(]*=`). Tested on seven headers: hwattention.hpp 9553cd0a11 first=37, device.hpp edec446b76 first=54 (`struct wqentry {`, the forward declaration at :48 no longer matches), alloc.hpp :24, model.hpp a9a9cf30a4 :61, mixture_of_experts.hpp 10fe891af5 :22, bf16.hpp 56d432ee61 :12, libpos.hpp 7206e88cc2 :98 (a constexpr function body). Verified: hw_prepare 467 (f59334dc24:1131-1597), 601 (edec446b76:1141-1741), 591 (a62d15a3dc:1141-1731); if at :1232, else at :1326, else end :1462; hunks 1237/1287/1322 -> first branch 54 lines, 1361/1419/1452 -> second branch 80 lines.

residual_risks: Trigger (a) narrowing (deleted pre-existing line) is set from one positive (PR 2176) and four negatives (1722, 2135, 2774, 4353); a future PR that adds a whole new mid-file block to an existing header has no precedent either way.

Trigger (d) thresholds (400 lines at BASE, 30 added lines, both branches) come from one example (hw_prepare 467 -> 601); step 5 was not run over the 48 silent PRs to see whether any grew a 400-line function without a comment. Insufficient data: run step 5 on the silent set.

The step 3 definition regex matches column-0 definitions only; a definition whose return type spans two lines, or a qualified name with spaces, would be missed and the prototype would be reported as having no definition (then the merged-taxonomy 'no consumer or definition' check owns it).
The step 2 first-body regex assumes clang-format style (`struct X {` on one line); a body whose `{` is on its own line would not count as the first body.
